A photograph, any photograph, has had the ISO (film speed) chosen, the aperture, shutter speed and framing. Framing is the most important part. Thus ALL photographs are fabricated. ALL of them. By definition a photograph cannot contain all the information present at its creation, thus it has been edited, thus it is a fabrication simply by existing.
Yet that's not what's being asked for.

The visible and perfectly linear sun seams are the big give away, but in general there's just a lot of things that don't "feel" right about the picture which are kind of hard to put your finger on. The obvious thing is the coloration, but also the shadows, fade rate, and blurring all seem off. The cloud pics on the left side of the image also seem distorted or to be of a lower resolution than the rest of the image. The wheat on the left side seems to be feeling a strong wind towards the left, yet the wheat on the right is perfectly fine. The wheat on the left side also has a much stronger blurring effect than anywhere else.

Given the errors all seem to be in segments my guess would be a composite of 3 heavily modified images. If that's not then case then I'd imagine it's a completely artificial rendering. I think there is close to 0 chance is a 'real' photograph.
